- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.2) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.1) — slightly raise forecast lows.
- Avoid overreacting to recent spikes — model tends to overshoot after sharp upward moves; dampen subsequent peaks.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Lagged sentiment influence: if sentiment was positive 3–5 days ago, adjust forecast downward slightly to avoid overconfidence.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early period (first 5–7 days) — cap initial forecast values at 10% below recent 14-day high.
- Don’t ignore sentiment momentum — if sentiment is rising (e.g., 0.27 → 0.32), reduce forecast slope to avoid runaway growth.
